title: Govt. races to new expressways | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 18 November 2026 00:00
-     - 57

By Charumini de Silva

The Cabinet of Ministers at its meeting on Monday approved construction contracts worth a combined Rs. 494.81 billion for two major expressway projects, involving the first phase of the Ruwanpura Expressway and the Kurunegala-Galewala section of the Central Expressway.

Announcing the decisions, Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said yesterday, the approvals cover a total of 23 construction packages, with 11 contrals valued at Rs. 251.37 billion for the Ruwanpura Expressway, and 12 other contracts worth Rs. 243.44 billion for the Central Expressway, where both totals are inclusive of Value Added Tax (VAT).

The allocation also represents nearly a quarter of the Government’s recently unveiled Rs. 2 trillion public capital expenditure push outlined under 2027 Budget last week by President and Finance Minister Anura Kumara Dissanayake to accelerate transport infrastructure development.

“Under the first phase of the Ruwanpura Expressway, the contracts cover the section from Kahathuduwa to Ingiriya, including the system interchange. The Cabinet initially approved construction of this phase on 27 July 2026, following which bids were invited through the National Competitive Procurement process,” he said at the weekly post-Cabinet meeting media briefing. 

International Construction Consortium Ltd., secured the largest contract, valued at Rs. 34.94 billion, followed by K.D.A. Weerasinghe and Co. Ltd., at Rs. 33.11 billion and NEM Construction Ltd., at Rs. 24.30 billion.

Access Engineering PLC was awarded two contracts worth Rs. 27.99 billion and Rs. 17.62 billion, while Maga Engineering Ltd., secured two worth Rs. 23.01 billion and Rs. 16.98 billion.

The remaining contracts went to Senura–Sanken joint venture worth Rs. 20.83 billion, Tudawe Brothers Ltd., worth Rs. 18.48 billion, RR Construction Ltd., worth Rs. 17.96 billion and Edward and Christie Ltd., worth Rs. 16.15 billion. 

He said the Central Expressway contracts cover the first phase of Section Four, spanning 38.5 km between Kurunegala and Galewala. The Cabinet of Ministers initially approved contruction of this section on 30 June 2026.

Accordingly, Maga Engineering Ltd., secured three contracts worth Rs. 14.15 billion, Rs. 26.28 billion and Rs. 24.45 billion.

NEM Construction Ltd., was awarded two contracts valued at Rs. 16.15 billion and Rs. 24.61 billion, while International Construction Consortium Ltd., secured two contracts worth Rs. 16.88 billion and Rs. 22.51 billion.

In addition, Edward and Christie Ltd., has been awarded a contract worth Rs. 18.39 billion, while K.D.A. Weerasinghe and Company Ltd., has secured a contract valued at Rs. 27.29 billion.

Tudawe Brothers Ltd., has been awarded a contract worth Rs. 14.44 billion, while RR Construction Ltd., secured a contract valued at Rs. 15.90 billion.

Access Engineering PLC has also been awarded a construction contract worth Rs. 22.39 billion.

Dr. Jayatissa said in both projects, the awards followed National Competitive Procurement procedures, bid evaluations and recommendations by the respective High-Level Procurement Committees. 

The Cabinet approved proposals submitted by Transport, Highways and Urban Development Minister Bimal Rathnayake.

title: Minister says two expressways  funded entirely by tax revenue | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 18 November 2026 00:29
-     - 7

In a post on ‘X’, the Minister noted the projects were “100% funded by tax revenue” with “zero loans”, adding that the Cabinet had given the green light for both expressways.

Rathnayake added, “People elected clean, capable leadership”, delivering for Sri Lanka.

title: Cabinet awards Rs. 7.36 b road contracts across Western  and Central provinces | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 18 November 2026 00:28
-     - 7

The Cabinet of Ministers has approved five road rehabilitation and improvement contracts worth Rs. 7.36 billion, covering rural roads in the Kalutara District and several key road sections under the National Highways Widening and Improvement Program and the program to reconstruct roads damaged by Cyclone Ditwah.

Under the Rural Road Program, two contracts covering rural road rehabilitation and improvement in the Kalutara District have been awarded to RR Construction Ltd., for Rs. 752.41 million and Rs. 773.33 million, respectively, excluding VAT.

Addressing the weekly post-Cabinet meeting media briefing yesterday, Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said the latest approvals complete the awarding of all five contract packages under this procurement exercise, for which 17 bids were received following a National Competitive Procurement process. 

He said the Cabinet had approved the first three contracts at its meeting on 21 September 2026, based on recommendations of the Higher Level Procurement Committee.

Separately, the Cabinet has approved three road development contracts under the National Highways Widening and Improvement Program and the program to reconstruct roads damaged by Cyclone Ditwah, following competitive bidding, with the contracts awarded to the lowest substantially responsive bidders on the recommendations of the respective High-Level Procurement Committees. 

Accordingly, Maga Engineering Ltd., has secured the largest contract, valued at Rs. 4.51 billion, for improving the 20 km road section from kilometre 38+970 to kilometre 59+000 of the Colombo-Ratnapura-Wellawaya-Batticaloa (AA004) Road, together with the 900-metre Avissawella Access Road and 100-metre Avissawella Town Road. The procurement attracted six bids.

In addition, Tudawe Brothers Ltd., has been awarded a Rs. 687.22 million contract for the rehabilitation and improvement of the 22.6 km Kelaniya-Mudungoda Road section from kilometre 6+500 to kilometre 29+100 in the Gampaha District, following the receipt of three bids.

Meanwhile, Sanguine Engineering Ltd., has secured a Rs. 635.87 million contract to restore damaged sections of the Peradeniya-Deltota-Rikillagaskada Road around kilometre 38, covering the junction of the 41st kilometre through to the 42nd kilometre. Five bids were received for the contract.

The Cabinet approved proposals submitted by Transport, Highways and Urban Development Minister Bimal Rathnayake.

title: Cyber Security under spotlight: CEO Forum today, full-day summit tomorrow | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 18 November 2026 00:25
-     - 7

The influential Cyber Security CEO Forum will be held today followed by the full-day Summit tomorrow, both at the Cinnamon Grand, Colombo bringing global and local experts together to highlight the impact of AI-powered attacks.

Held for the 12th consecutive year, the premier Cyber Security Summit is co-hosted by the Daily FT and CICRA under the theme “Unthinkable Threats: AI, Quantum and Sri Lanka’s Digital Siege.”

Giving high prominence to the twin events, President’s Chief Advisor on Digital Economy and GovTec Chairman Dr. Hans Wijayasuriya will attend tonight’s CEO Forum whilst Digital Economy Deputy Minister Eng. Eranga Weeraratne and Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe will be present at the full-day summit tomorrow.

The twin events are designed to provide the insights, solutions, and hands on experience needed to confront the AI-driven threat landscape head on, bringing together business leaders, cybersecurity professionals, and technology experts from across the region.

The CEO Forum (by invitation only) will tackle the issue of “Leading through AI-powered cyber attacks” (Is your organization ready for AI-based cyber attacks?).

Other speakers include Resecurity, Head of SAARC Rajan Patan, Broadcom Tanzu Division Head of Asia Pacific and Japan Michael Fishman, Brandix Director Oshada Senanayake and CICRA Holdings Group Executive Director/CEO Boshan Dayaratne.

Organisers said addressing board level liability under the Companies Act and the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA), and the urgent need for robust AI governance frameworks. This exclusive forum is tailored for C-suite executives and board members, emphasising that cyber security is no longer an IT issue but a strategic business imperative. The CEO Forum will examine why boardroom engagement is essential for proactive defence, how directors and senior leaders must take ownership of cyber risk, set the tone for organisational resilience, and ensure that AI governance is embedded at the highest level. It will also discuss practical frameworks for anticipating AI-powered threats rather than merely reacting to breaches, and how boards can foster a culture of security that permeates every layer of the organisation.

The summit tomorrow (by prior registration https://cybersecuritysummit.lk) will bring together global experts, industry leaders, and policymakers through four critical sessions.

“The Digital Trust Crisis: Fraud Defence, Identity Security and Citizen Protection” session will see a keynote by Resecurity, Head of SAARC Rajan Patan whilst MAS Holdings Group Chief Digital Officer Steve Dodd will be the Guest Speaker. Panellists are Central Bank of Sri Lanka CISO Sanjee Balasuriya, Cyber Command and Information Warfare Centre Director Defence Brigadier K.V.P. Dhammika USAP and HNB CISO Suresh Emmanuel.

Session on “AI at the frontline: From weaponised intelligence to AI governance” will include keynote by Tanzu Business Unit | VMware by Broadcom Solution Architect Eknath Reddy and Guest speech by Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Prof. Hareendra Dissabandara. Panellists are Fortitude Associate Vice President, IT infrastructure and Cyber security Prageeth Kapuruge and MillenniumIT ESP Senior Director – Cybersecurity/Managed Security Services Musthaq Mukthar.

Session 3 will be “When prevention fails: Building cyber resilience in an AI accelerated work” with EY GDS Sri Lanka Senior Manager Kumudh Pathirana as keynote speaker and Bank of Ceylon CISCO Iresh Ratnayake as Guest Speaker. Panellists will be Nestle Lanka Assistant Director/Head of Legal and Regulatory Keerthi Pathiraja and D. Samsons and Sons Senior Deputy General Manager IT and Digital Transformation Dr. Aloka Jayawardene.

Final session titled “Defending the Digital Nation: Sri Lanka’s Cyber Strategy and Resilience Building” will see GovTec CEO Shevan Goonetilleke delivering the keynote ad Sri Lanka Police Director IT SSP Laksiri Geethal as Guest Speaker. Panellists are Data Privacy AI Governance and Technology Contracts  Gayanthi Gunawardene, Brandix Director Oshada Senanayake and People’s Bank CISCO Lasantha Thenuwara.

The Summit will conclude with the famous “Night Hack” event which delivers a thrilling night of AI hacking and defending, giving participants a live, hands-on look at the real-world implications of AI-powered threats. Together, the two events will provide the insights, solutions, and experience needed to build resilience against the next generation of cyber risks.

 For registration and more information, please visit https://cybersecuritysummit.lk 

Strategic partner is Resecurity, Platinum partner EY GDS Sri Lanka, Gold Partner VMWare by Broadcom, Official Banking Partner Bank of Ceylon, Hospitality Partner Cinnamon Grand, Brand Communications Partner BBDO Sri Lanka.

title: Sigma7 investigation finds no evidence to substantiate $ 250 million X-Press Pearl bribery allegation | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 18 November 2026 00:24
-     - 23

An independent investigation has found no evidence to substantiate or corroborate the allegation that London P&I and/or, X-Press Feeders, the Owners of the MV X-Press Pearl, paid a $ 250 million bribe to influence actions of Sri Lankan authorities in the context of compensation pursued by the government as a result of the sinking of the MV X-Press Pearl in 2021.

Sigma7 Business Intelligence, a leading business intelligence and investigations firm, has published its findings in An investigation into the $250 million X-Press Pearl Bribery Allegation. The investigation was commissioned by London P&I, the vessel’s liability insurer, on behalf of the Owners of the X-Press Pearl, to investigate this very serious accusation.

The full report is available at Sigma7 investigation finds no evidence to substantiate US$250 million X-Press Pearl bribery allegation

In May 2021, the container ship MV X-Press Pearl caught fire, and ultimately sank on 2 June off the coast of Sri Lanka. The incident released plastic pellets, known as nurdles, and other debris into the sea. Following the incident, teams were mobilised to clean up the pollution, and the wreck was subsequently removed. 

The incident led to legal proceedings in several jurisdictions. These included:  Fundamental rights petitions before Sri Lanka’s Supreme Court against the vessel’s owners, operators, and local agent, alongside government authorities;  A compensation claim brought by the Sri Lankan government in Singapore;  and Proceedings in the English Admiralty Court concerning the right to limit liability. 

Following the sinking and while the various legal proceedings were underway, in April 2023 the then Minister of Justice, Prison Affairs and Constitutional Reforms Wijeyadasa Rajapakshe said  he had received information that a $250 million bribe had been paid to influence the X-Press Pearl compensation efforts pursued by Sri Lanka. 

The allegation was subsequently repeated in parliament, in media coverage and during proceedings before Sri Lanka’s Supreme Court. These reports gave differing accounts of the alleged recipient and the destination of the funds.

As part of the investigation, Sigma7 Business Intelligence reviewed parliamentary speeches, publicly available court records, English- and Sinhala-language media reporting as well as multiple specialist and subscription-only databases covering credit information, company ownership and directorships, and property interests. 

The investigation traced the allegation’s origins and examined how successive accounts changed as it circulated through political statements and media coverage. Sigma7 researched the backgrounds and known assets of individuals named in connection with the allegation, it also tested the validity of the purported bank-account details. 

The report concluded that there was no evidence substantiating the alleged payment by either London P&I or the Owners of the X-Press Pearl. The investigation identified significant gaps in the information on which the allegation was based.

The allegation originated from an anonymous WhatsApp message. Yet the original message, its sender and the telephone number from which it originated have never been publicly disclosed. 

The $250 million was alleged to have been paid into a NatWest bank account in the UK, details of which were published in the Supreme Court judgment. The purported account details were inconsistent, and Sigma7 Business Intelligence’s attempts to make nominal payments to reconstructed versions of the account were unsuccessful. 

The report also highlights the scrutiny that a transfer of $250 million would face under UK anti-money-laundering controls, including checks on the parties involved, the source of the funds and the purpose of the transaction. UK banks are required to report known or suspected money laundering, including where there are reasonable grounds for suspicion.

Versions of the allegation also indicate that the destination of the alleged bribe moved from a NatWest account in the UK to an unidentified account in the Bahamas, for which no verifiable banking details were provided. 

The identity of the alleged intermediary/recipient of the bribe also shifted. Initial references to a relative of an Attorney General’s Department officer were followed by the naming of “Chamara Gunasekara”, whom subsequent media reporting identified as Manju/Manjusiri Nissanka/Nishshanka. Nishshanka publicly and categorically denied the claim. Lanka eNews later withdrew its reporting and issued an apology. 

Lastly, even those responsible for publicising the allegation expressed reservations about its reliability. Ajith Mannapperuma, the Member of Parliament who originally claimed to have received the allegation via WhatsApp and who later forwarded it to Rajapakshe, said he had not believed the original message because he could find no supporting evidence. 

Former Head of the Metropolitan Police’s Counter Terrorism Command Richard Walton in a statement said: “Having reviewed Sigma7’s investigation and the methodology underpinning its findings, I fully endorse its central conclusion: there is no credible evidence whatsoever to substantiate the allegation that London P&I, or X-Press Feeders, the Owners of the MV X-Press Pearl, paid a $250 million bribe to influence compensation proceedings arising from the sinking of the MV X-Press Pearl. 

The report does more than establish an absence of supporting evidence. It exposes fundamental inconsistencies and contradictions in the allegation itself, including demonstrably flawed bank account details, conflicting accounts of the alleged recipient and the purported destination of the funds. Taken together, these findings seriously undermine the credibility of the original accusation. 

As a former Head of the United Kingdom Metropolitan Police’s Counter Terrorism Command, I understand the critical distinction between intelligence, allegation and established fact. An anonymous, uncorroborated claim may justify further investigation, but it cannot reasonably be treated as evidence of wrongdoing. Nor does its repetition in Parliament, the media or official proceedings confer upon it any greater credibility.”

title: Home Lands awards construction of Central Park Boulevard Port City Colombo to CHEC | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 18 November 2026 00:23
-     - 7

Home Lands Group Chairman Nalin Herath (right) exchanging the agreement with CHEC South Asia and South East Asia Managing Director Wang Gang

Home Lands Group has awarded the construction of its landmark 40-storey twin-tower development project at Port City Colombo, Central Park Boulevard to the world-renowned China Harbour Engineering Company (CHEC) in a major construction, conceptual and structural design collaboration.

The strategic construction collaboration between Home Lands and CHEC began earlier this year with Home Lands awarding the construction of its iconic mega project Pentara Residencies Thummulla Handiya to CHEC. 

The construction of Central Park Boulevard Port City Colombo being undertaken by CHEC marks the second time Home Lands has placed its trust on CHEC to deliver a world class product based on CHEC’s expertise and impressive track record. The agreement was signed by Home Lands Group Chairman Nalin Herath and CHEC South Asia and South East Asia Managing Director Wang Gang.

As one of the world’s leading engineering and construction companies, CHEC brings decades of expertise across Asia, Africa, Europe and the Middle East. Its work across ports, highways, bridges and large-scale reclamation projects has earned the company a global reputation for quality, scale and timely delivery.

The architecture of Central Park Boulevard Port City Colombo has been designed by SOG Architects (Singapore) and PWA Architects (Sri Lanka). SOG Architects, an internationally acclaimed design studio with experience across Asia, Europe and the Middle East, brings global design excellence, blending timeless architecture, refined spatial planning and contemporary luxury. PWA Architects, one of the country’s respected architectural practices, brings deep local insight, ensuring the design responds to Sri Lanka’s climate, culture and way of life.

The interiors have been curated by Blaine Robert Design, the acclaimed Malaysian studio renowned for sophisticated residential, hospitality, retail and commercial environments across the region. With over three decades of design and build expertise, the studio brings timeless elegance, bespoke detailing and meticulous craftsmanship to every residence and shared space.

The Principal Structural Engineer of Central Park Boulevard Port City Colombo is East China Architectural Design and Research Institute (ECADI), one of China’s foremost design institutes, with work spanning supertall towers such as Tianjin 117 and Wuhan Centre, major transport hubs including Shanghai Pudong International Airport, and projects across 23 countries. The structural design is independently peer reviewed by Meinhardt Singapore, part of the global Meinhardt Group with over 4,500 specialists across Asia, Australia, the Middle East and Europe, ensuring every structural element meets the highest international standards.

Nalin Herath said: “Central Park Boulevard Port City Colombo sets a new benchmark for luxury living in Sri Lanka. For every element of this development, we have engaged the finest expertise in the world, and Home Lands brings these elements together under one vision and one standard. Our customers deserve a true masterpiece, and that is what we are delivering. With construction progressing ahead of schedule, we are on track to complete the project in 36 months.”

The piling works of Central Park Boulevard Port City Colombo were completed in just 88 days, against the six months originally planned, by three leading contractors: Access Engineering PLC, Sanken Construction’s San Piling (Pvt) Ltd., and D P Jayasinghe Piling Company (Pvt) Ltd. Completing piling in less than half the scheduled time marks a major early milestone.

Overlooking and merging with the 40-acre Central Park, Central Park Boulevard Port City Colombo rises as high-end, ultra-luxury 40-storey twin towers, designed to become a defining landmark on the Colombo skyline. Every resident enjoys a choice of sweeping views of the parkland, the Indian Ocean and the city, along with world-class amenities. Its global lifestyle is inspired by one of the world’s most renowned luxury lifestyle brands. Backed by world-class partners at every stage, Central Park Boulevard Port City Colombo is a true reflection of the Home Lands promise: Trust, Innovation and Excellence.

title: CNCI commends Budget 2027 focus on production economy and SMEs | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 18 November 2026 00:22
-     - 22

The Ceylon National Chamber of Industries (CNCI), has commended the Government’s 2027 Budget focus on production economy and SMEs but called for urgent action on industrial cost relief and trade reforms.

CNCI Chairman Pradeep Kahawalage acknowledged that the National Budget 2027 was thoughtfully designed around key priorities, including preserving macroeconomic stability, enhancing the economy’s resilience, revitalising the rural economy, and ensuring stability in energy markets.

Kahawalage emphasised the President’s vision of delivering a Budget that “strengthens the production economy, protects small and medium-scale industries, makes room for investment, connects knowledge and technology to the economy through digital economic activities, protects the environment, and ensures social justice.”

He further noted that the Government’s recognition of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) as the cornerstone of rapid economic transformation is a vital step forward. In particular, the allocation of Rs. 67,687 million for interest subsidies and refinancing, expected to unlock Rs. 174 billion in concessionary loans to entrepreneurs through state and private banks, provides a timely boost to enterprise development.

On industrial infrastructure, Kahawalage welcomed the targeted allocations to develop the Valachchenai Industrial Estate, conduct feasibility studies and preliminary planning for the Puliyankulam Industrial Estate, and accelerate ongoing development across new industrial zones in Ingiriya, Dambulla, Raigama, Millaniya, and Katunayake. Combined with infrastructure upgrades in existing estates, these initiatives lay a strong foundation for near-term industrial expansion.

The President’s initiative to drive digital transformation and transition into a Digital Era is also highly commendable. The “Digitalisation serves as a foundational tool for modernising public administration, improving the efficiency and transparency of Government activities, and strengthening institutional capacity”.

The Chairman CNCI, also noted that the Government officials have the ultimate responsibility of properly utilisation of the allocated funds for the infrastructure development projects “transport, highways, railways, water supply, irrigation, health, education, housing, urban development, energy, digital infrastructure, ports, and decentralised regional projects” to fulfill the Presidents objective of the Budget “to move from economic stability towards transformation”. To ensure the timely utilisation of allocated capital, the Government must enforce disciplined governance reforms across the project lifecycle.

However, representing the broader manufacturing and industrial community, the CNCI Chairman also highlighted several critical gaps and drawbacks in Budget 2027 that require urgent policy attention to ensure local industries remain competitive; the Budget lacks “broad-based relief on industrial power tariffs or corporate taxes to ease operational pressures on domestic factories”, “removal of the Simplified Value Added Tax (SVAT) scheme”, “major flagship industrial or construction mega-projects capable of driving large-scale private-sector participation and downstream manufacturing demand”.

He reaffirmed the Chamber’s unwavering commitment and cooperation with the Government in its journey toward sustainable prosperity and peace based on a shared national vision, while extending his congratulations to the President on the presentation of Budget 2027.

title: Cabinet clears Rs. 5.96 b Oliyamulla pumping station to curb Kelani River flood risk | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 18 November 2026 00:04
-     - 2

Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa

In a bid to reduce flood risks in the Mudun Ela water catchment, the Cabinet of Ministers has approved Stage I of the Oliyamulla pumping station project at a total estimated cost of Rs. 5,962.13 million, to be implemented from 2027 to 2031, Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said.

The canal system of the Mudun Ela catchment connects to the Kelani River at Oliyamulla, Peliyagoda and Pethiyagoda. When the upper regions of the river flood, water enters these urban areas through the canals, exposing low-lying lands in the catchment to flooding.

Studies recommended building a pumping station at Oliyamulla, where the catchment’s main canal meets the river, to minimise the risk.

The project is planned to be implemented with financing from the Government of Sri Lanka and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), with pumping stations of a combined 35 m³/s capacity. Stage I will deliver a 15 m³/s station, while Stage II will add a 20 m³/s station.

The Cabinet approved proposals submitted by Transport, Highways and Urban Development Minister Bimal Rathnayake.

title: Met. Dept. warns of haze, poorer air quality as cyclonic storm Akvan shifts winds | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 18 November 2026 00:02
-     - 4

The Department of Meteorology has warned that air quality across Sri Lanka could worsen and hazy conditions could persist over the next few days. It said changes in wind patterns caused by Cyclonic Storm Akvan are behind the conditions.

A Department official said the unusual haze over Colombo comes from winds that the cyclonic system is pushing towards Sri Lanka from the direction of India. The official said current atmospheric conditions could lower air quality in several parts of the country in the coming days.

The haze is expected to be most noticeable at night and in the early morning, though it could also develop at times in the afternoon. The Department said mist could form alongside the haze and reduce visibility, and it urged the public to stay vigilant while the conditions last.

title: Cabinet raises Aswesuma empowerment grants to Rs. 200,000, expands beneficiaries by 525 | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 18 November 2026 00:01
-     - 1

The Cabinet of Ministers has approved an increase in capital grants for eligible low-income families under the World Bank-funded Social Security Project, raising the maximum allocation from Rs. 150,000 to Rs. 200,000 while expanding the targeted beneficiaries from 10,975 to 11,500 families.

Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said move was approved following the World Bank’s agreement to enhance the financial assistance and expand the program based on experience gained during its first phase.

The initiative, targeting poor and extremely poor families receiving Aswesuma welfare benefits, is being implemented with funding support from the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank (ADB). Under the ADB-funded component, capital grants have already been disbursed to 8,660 families, concluding the program implemented through that facility.

Under the World Bank-funded Social Security Project, 4,900 families across seven districts have received capital grants during the first phase. A further 6,600 families identified across five districts were initially earmarked for assistance in the second phase.

He said the revised arrangements will increase the overall number of families targeted for empowerment under the World Bank project to 11,500, while raising the maximum grant available to eligible beneficiary households to Rs. 200,000.

The Cabinet had initially approved the broader program at its meeting on 13 October 2025, with the objective of supporting vulnerable households to strengthen their economic resilience and move towards sustainable livelihoods.

The proposal to this effect was approved the proposal submitted by the Rural Development, Social Security and Community Empowerment Minister Dr. Upali Pannilage.

title: US Court strikes down Trump plan to cap stay of foreign students, journalists | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 18 November 2026 00:00
-     - 2

A US federal court has struck down a Trump administration proposal to cap the amount of time foreign students, scholars, and journalists can spend in the country on their respective visas.

In July, the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) proposed a policy aimed at preventing international students from staying in the country for more than four years unless they obtained federal approval.

Boston federal Judge F. Dennis Saylor delivered a ruling on Monday striking down the DHS proposal as “arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, and otherwise not in accordance with law.”

“Put bluntly, DHS is seeking to prevent or discourage the very activity — providing educational opportunities for foreign students in the United States — that Congress sought to permit and encourage,” Judge Saylor said in his ruling.

 “The statute simply does not grant DHS such broad and open-ended authority to undermine the F-1 visa program,” he added.

The proposed rule also sought to shorten how long foreign journalists can stay in the country from several years to 240 days or 90 days for Chinese journalists.

The proposed rule also shortened the grace period – the window to depart after finishing studies or post-completion OPT from 60 days to 30.

For language programmes, there was an aggregate limit of 24 months for stays, including breaks and vacations.

One of the lead plaintiffs, Presidents’ Alliance on Higher Education and Education President and CEO Miriam Feldblum termed the federal court ruling as a clear and important victory for international students and scholars and the colleges and universities that welcome them.

 “The harmful consequences of the current administration’s policy actions and efforts are already evident in the significant declines in international student enrolment and interest we are witnessing,” Feldblum said in a statement.

 “With this ruling, the judge has sent an unequivocal and resounding message: the longstanding Duration of Status policy is retained,” said Fanta Aw, Executive Director and CEO of NAFSA: Association of International Educators.
